subject: AWS private offer: Acme Corp request — rev-share & non-standard discount approval
messages:
From: Laura Jenkins <laura.jenkins@acme-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: AWS private offer + term sheet (Acme)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Acme is ready to move to a private offer on AWS to standardize procurement. Attached is a draft PO and our preferred term sheet (see AWS_Private_Offer_Term_Sheet.docx). High level asks:

- 18 month contract term, start date on signature
- One-time onboarding credit request equivalent to a 30% discount in year 1 (we call it a launch rebate)
- AWS will collect and remit marketplace rev-share; Acme is asking we accept marketplace-standard rev-share (they expect ~14%) but they want the redwood list and invoice to show the reduced net price to Acme
- Clarify data residency and audit obligations (Acme is EU-facing but will purchase via US account)

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to the 18-month private offer and the discount structure? Also routing note: Acme procurement needs an exec approval for discounts exceeding 25% and any non-standard marketplace term.

Appreciate a quick timeline — they hope to close next week.

Best,
Laura
Procurement Lead, Acme Corp
[Attachment: Acme_PO_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: AWS private offer + term sheet (Acme)

Team — forwarding Acme's request. Key deviations from standard: 18mo term, launch rebate ~30% (year 1 net), and marketplace will expect ~14% rev-share to AWS. Per Deal Desk policy, discounts >25% and any marketplace rev-share over 12% need exec approval.

Proposed options to present:
- Option A (accelerate close): 30% launch rebate year 1, 14% AWS rev-share, 18mo term. Requires exec signoff for discount + partner rev-share exception.
- Option B (policy-aligned): 22% launch rebate, 12% rev-share, 12mo term + optional 6mo extension. Legal would need to adjust the termination notice.

Requesting: Marissa/Vivek — can you triage approval path? Jordan — can you prelim review the term sheet for any non-starters (liability/data residency)? Acme wants a signed doc by 7/6.

Attaching Acme PO and term sheet for reference.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec — Strategic Sales
[Attachment: AWS_Private_Offer_Term_Sheet.docx (docx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: AWS private offer + term sheet (Acme)

Karthik — thanks for the summary. Commercial view: Acme is strategic and high-velocity; I'm comfortable escalating.

Initial stance: I can approve up to 30% launch rebate on the condition that:
- Finance signs off on ARR recognition and the accounting treatment of the rebate
- We secure AWS confirmation in writing on rev-share mechanics (so revenue reporting remains clean)
- We lock an 18-month committed ARR that justifies the concession (minimum annual commitment numbers in PO)

Vivek — need your partner OK on the 14% rev-share to AWS. If you can accept the 14% with a marketing co-fund (e.g., AWS credits or co-marketing $) we can push Option A.

Jordan — please flag any legal blockers (data residency, audit scope, termination for convenience). If Legal needs more time, call out the minimum redlines.

-Marissa
VP, Sales Operations

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: AWS private offer + term sheet (Acme)

Marissa/Karthik — I reviewed partner economics. I can approve AWS rev-share at 14% for this private offer provided we get two things from AWS and Acme before signature:

1) Written confirmation from AWS Marketplace on how the 14% will be applied and that the net pricing shown to Acme is compatible with our revenue recognition (we need the flow documented).
2) A marketing co-fund from Acme or AWS (preferably AWS credits) to offset the effective first-year CAC and to help us feature a case study. Equivalent minimum co-fund: $60k.

Operational asks: billing must route via AWS Marketplace so we have marketplace receipts; Legal (Jordan) to add a 90-day audit window (no broad unlimited access) and a limited data residency statement (we will store EU customer data in EU region instances).

If those conditions are met, I give partner approval for 14% rev-share and Marissa can approve the 30% launch rebate.

-Vivek
Head of Partnerships

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: AWS private offer + term sheet (Acme)

Team — quick legal read attached; high-level redlines required before we sign Option A:

- Data residency clause: We will commit to EU region processing for EU-customer PII only; global aggregate telemetry remains cross-region.
- Audit scope: limit to 90-day lookback, scoped to invoice verification and SOC-type artifacts; no production access.
- Termination and liability: carve out a 6-month wind-down on long-term commitments and cap liability at $1M or 2x fees (whichever is lower).
- Marketplace mechanics: require AWS written confirmation on rev-share flow and tax treatment.

If Acme accepts these redlines, Legal can sign off and I will prepare a short amendment for the PO. Also recommend we include an explicit clause that discounts are one-time launch rebates, not a change to list pricing, to avoid future price-expectation issues.

Send me the finalized PO and I will prep DocuSign.

-Jordan
Principal Counsel

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Jenkins <laura.jenkins@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 15:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: AWS private offer + term sheet (Acme) — Next steps and exec approvals

Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround. Good news: commercial and partner leads have provisionally approved Option A (30% launch rebate, 14% AWS rev-share, 18mo term) subject to the following items being confirmed before signature:

1) AWS to provide written confirmation of rev-share flow and that marketplace billing will produce receipts compatible with Redwood revenue recognition. (AWS sales looped here — can you confirm in-thread?)
2) Acme or AWS to commit marketing co-fund of $60k (can be AWS credits).
3) Legal redlines as below (Jordan): 90-day audit scope, EU-only data residency for PII, 6-month wind-down and liability cap.

If you can confirm (1–3) by COB Monday (7/6) we will route the DocuSign and OK for sign-off. Attaching the redline checklist and our proposed amendment.

Next steps on our side: Jordan will prepare the amendment once we have AWS confirmation; Marissa will OK final commercial; Vivek will confirm partner acceptance. I will circulate the DocuSign link once Legal signs off.

Thanks — excited to get Acme live on AWS Marketplace.

Best,
Karthik
Account Exec — Strategic Sales
[Attachment: Redwood_Acme_Amendment_Redlines.pdf (pdf)]
